description: A noise source offering seven colours of noise at once plus a Perlin noise generator with four octaves

params.text: Sets how fast the Perlin noise moves, 1 to 500; it comes up in the middle at 250
Attenuverts the voltage at the Perlin speed input before it is added to the PERLIN knob; at full clockwise 5V covers the whole speed range
Sets the amplitude of the Perlin noise and of its four octave outputs, 1 to 13; it comes up at 1
Attenuverts the voltage at the Perlin amplifier input before it is added to the P. AMP knob; at full clockwise 5V covers the whole amplifier range
Sets how much that octave counts towards the Perlin noise mix, 0% to 100%; all four come up at 25%, and the mix is their weighted average

inputs.text: Shifts the Perlin speed; the voltage is divided by 5, multiplied by 500 and by the attenuverter beside it, then added to the PERLIN knob and held between 1 and 500
Shifts the Perlin amplifier; the voltage is divided by 5, multiplied by 13 and by the attenuverter beside it, then added to the P. AMP knob and held between 1 and 13

outputs.text: The weighted mix of all four Perlin octaves, its ring shaded white through grey
The Perlin noise at that octave on its own; the panel marks each octave with its multiple of the PERLIN speed, *1, *2, 4* and 8*
White noise, equal power at every frequency
Grey noise, shaped to an inverted A-weighting curve so it sounds equally loud across the band
Uniform random numbers spread evenly from -5V to +5V, which the maker calls Prism; its ring is multicoloured

notes: A noise colour is only generated while a cable is in its jack, so the unused outputs cost nothing.

inputs.0:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 1 to 500V.
inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 1 to 13V.
